answer: The willow multiplier is published, charged in ferrous, and prism lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every participant already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4947 identities would post 3093 proofs and burn roughly 84 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
